neighbours.label: the final word-piece of a French-style surname split by the tokenizer after a Boud-/Grand-/Bour-/Baud- stem (Bou·din, Gran·din, Bour·don, Bure·l)
fire: The lecture by Temple Grandin drew a large crowd of ranchers.
A beach scene by Eugène Boudin sold for a record price.
The new book from Dr. Grandin explains how cattle see the world.
Monet learned to paint outdoors from his mentor Boudin in Normandy.
The expedition led by Nicolas Baudin mapped the southern coast.
The paper by Lortholary and Boudon appeared in a medical journal.
The model proposed by Kindlmann and Burel is widely cited.
The toxicology study by Bourdon and colleagues was published in 2012.
quiet: The lecture by Temple Smith drew a large crowd of ranchers.
A beach scene by Claude Monet sold for a record price.
The new book from Dr. Martin explains how cattle see the world.
Monet learned to paint outdoors from his mentor Robert in Normandy.
The expedition led by Nicolas Dupont mapped the southern coast.
The paper by Laurent and Bernard appeared in a medical journal.
The model proposed by Fischer and Wilson is widely cited.
The toxicology study by Thomas and colleagues was published in 2012.

notes: Card: 'in' x5, 'l' x3, 'on' x2, 'don' x2 after Boud/Bour/Grand; ' definition' x7 is a weaker second trigger (probe 'By definition' 0.13-0.35) and is not tested here. Probes: Grandin 1.08, Boudin 0.64, Bourdon/Burel 0.51, Baudin/Jardin 0.36, Gaudin/Bourdin 0.25, Hardin/Sandin 0.21, Martin 0.005.
